A fire has gutted a warehouse belonging to a popular tyre distributor, Alhaji Yakubu Ibrahim, along Katsina Road in Kaduna metropolis, triggering panic among traders and residents in the area.
The incident occurred on Monday evening at the warehouse located near Lagos Street, a major commercial hub in Kaduna North Local Government Area.
Eyewitnesses said the fire started at about 4:00 p.m. and rapidly spread through the facility, destroying tyres and other automobile accessories stored inside.
The warehouse belongs to Ibrahim, an accredited distributor of Michelin tyres, and reportedly contained hundreds of tyres and other valuable goods.
The inferno, fuelled by highly flammable materials in the warehouse, initially defied efforts by residents and traders to put it out, prompting distress calls to the Kaduna State Fire Service.
Thick smoke billowing from the warehouse threw the area into confusion as traders and residents scrambled to salvage their goods and prevent the fire from spreading to adjoining shops and buildings.
However, personnel of the Kaduna State Fire Service arrived at the scene and brought the situation under control, preventing the fire from spreading further.
As of the time of filing this report, firefighters were still at the scene working to extinguish the remaining flames and ensure that no embers were left.
Some tyres were reportedly salvaged through the combined efforts of residents and fellow traders before the fire consumed them.
Although the cause of the fire had yet to be established, the financial losses were estimated to run into millions of naira.
Meanwhile, police personnel from the Magaji Gari Division were deployed to the scene to maintain law and order and prevent hoodlums from taking advantage of the incident to loot shops and warehouses.
Residents commended the swift intervention of the fire service and police, while calling on the Kaduna State Government to provide additional firefighting equipment in markets and other busy commercial centres.
Efforts to speak with the warehouse owner, Alhaji Yakubu Ibrahim, were unsuccessful as he was said to be traumatised by the incident.
